concepts.name: EBITDA
concepts.one_line: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization: the rough cash-earnings number every leverage and coverage ratio is built on, before creditors adjust it.
concepts.moyer: Ch. 3, financial analysis of the distressed firm

concepts.name: Enterprise value
concepts.one_line: What the whole business is worth to all its capital providers together; value fills the capital structure from the top, and where it runs out decides who gets paid.
concepts.moyer: Ch. 6, valuation of the reorganized firm

concepts.name: Working capital
concepts.one_line: Inventory plus receivables minus payables: the cash tied up in running the business day to day, and the first thing to seize up when vendors stop shipping.

concepts.name: Liquidity
concepts.one_line: Cash plus what can still be drawn on the revolver: the runway a company has before it must file, refinance or do a deal.

concepts.name: Leverage
concepts.one_line: Debt divided by EBITDA: how many years of earnings it would take to repay the debt, and the ratio covenants and rating agencies watch.

concepts.name: Secured versus unsecured debt
concepts.one_line: Secured debt has a claim on specific collateral and is paid from it first; unsecured debt has only the borrower's promise and shares in what is left.
concepts.moyer: Ch. 4, the capital structure and where value breaks

concepts.name: Collateral
concepts.one_line: The specific assets pledged to a lender, which that lender can be paid from ahead of everyone else.

concepts.name: Lien
concepts.one_line: The legal claim a secured lender holds over collateral; first lien is paid first, second lien next, from the same assets.

concepts.name: Asset-based loan (ABL)
concepts.one_line: A revolver whose availability is a percentage of eligible inventory and receivables, so the lender with the smallest claim can control the company's cash.

concepts.name: Borrowing base
concepts.one_line: The formula that sets how much an ABL lender will lend: eligible inventory and receivables times advance rates, minus reserves the agent can impose.

concepts.name: Revolving credit facility
concepts.one_line: A bank line that can be drawn, repaid and redrawn; the first place a company reaches for liquidity and the first lender to notice trouble.

concepts.name: Term loan
concepts.one_line: A loan drawn once and repaid on a schedule or at maturity, usually secured and usually held by institutions rather than banks.

concepts.name: Indenture
concepts.one_line: The contract governing a bond issue: the coupon, maturity, covenants, guarantees and what counts as a default.
concepts.moyer: Ch. 5, legal aspects of the indenture

concepts.name: Covenant
concepts.one_line: A promise in a loan or bond document about what the borrower must do or may not do, whose breach lets lenders act.

concepts.name: Guarantee
concepts.one_line: A promise by another entity, usually a parent or subsidiary, to pay a debt if the borrower does not, which pulls a claim up to that entity.

concepts.name: Structural subordination
concepts.one_line: A claim at a parent company is paid only from what is left after the subsidiary's own creditors are paid, because the subsidiary's assets belong to the subsidiary.

concepts.name: Intercreditor agreement
concepts.one_line: The contract among lender groups fixing who is first on which collateral, who gets paid in what order, and who controls remedies.

concepts.name: Payment waterfall
concepts.one_line: The order in which proceeds are distributed: each layer is paid in full before the next receives anything.

concepts.name: First-out / second-out / third-out
concepts.one_line: A payment order among lenders sharing one lien: they hold the same collateral but agree by contract who is paid first from it.
concepts.moyer: not in Moyer by name; extends the intercreditor idea

concepts.name: Liability management exercise (LME)
concepts.one_line: An out-of-court transaction that changes who ranks where or raises new money without a bankruptcy filing, often at the expense of non-participating lenders.
concepts.moyer: Ch. 9, out-of-court exchanges, extended to modern LMEs

concepts.name: Exchange offer
concepts.one_line: An offer to swap existing bonds or loans for new instruments, usually with a discount, a longer maturity or a better ranking, to avoid a filing.

concepts.name: Special purpose vehicle (SPV)
concepts.one_line: A subsidiary created to issue debt or hold assets so the new paper can rank ahead of the existing lenders' claims on the parent.

concepts.name: On-loan
concepts.one_line: An intercompany loan passing bond proceeds from an SPV issuer down to the operating company, which creates a claim the SPV lenders sit behind.

concepts.name: Priming lien
concepts.one_line: A new lien placed ahead of existing liens on the same collateral, which the Bankruptcy Code allows for a DIP if the old lenders are adequately protected.

concepts.name: Chapter 11
concepts.one_line: The U.S. reorganization chapter: the company keeps operating under court protection while it negotiates a plan that binds its creditors.

concepts.name: DIP financing
concepts.one_line: Debtor-in-possession loans made after a filing with a court-ordered superpriority claim and usually priming liens; whoever writes the DIP often ends up owning the company.

concepts.name: Roll-up
concepts.one_line: Converting a lender's pre-petition claims into DIP claims as a condition of new money, which lifts old debt to the front of the line.

concepts.name: Payment in kind (PIK)
concepts.one_line: Interest or a fee paid by adding it to principal rather than in cash, which saves cash today and makes the claim grow.

concepts.name: Backstop premium
concepts.one_line: A fee paid to lenders who commit to fund whatever other lenders decline to, in exchange for guaranteeing the deal gets done.

concepts.name: Milestones
concepts.one_line: Dated case steps written into a DIP or RSA, whose miss is a default that hands the lenders control of the timetable.

concepts.name: Term SOFR
concepts.one_line: The floating-rate benchmark that replaced LIBOR; DIP and revolver pricing is quoted as a spread over it.

concepts.name: Critical vendor
concepts.one_line: A supplier the court lets the debtor pay on pre-petition claims because the business cannot run without it, jumping that vendor ahead of other unsecureds.

concepts.name: Unsecured creditors' committee (UCC)
concepts.one_line: The court-appointed body that represents general unsecured creditors and negotiates or fights for their recovery.

concepts.name: Litigation trust
concepts.one_line: A vehicle set up by a plan to hold the estate's lawsuits for the benefit of a creditor class, so a recovery can come later from litigation.

concepts.name: Marshaling
concepts.one_line: The equitable rule that a creditor with two sources of recovery can be required to exhaust one before touching the pool another creditor depends on.

concepts.name: Disclosure statement
concepts.one_line: The court-approved voting document for a plan: valuation, recoveries by class, the liquidation analysis and the risks.
concepts.moyer: Ch. 12, the plan and disclosure statement

concepts.name: Restructuring support agreement (RSA)
concepts.one_line: A contract in which creditors agree to support a plan on stated terms and milestones before it is filed or launched.

concepts.name: Impaired class
concepts.one_line: A class of claims that does not get paid in full or on its original terms under a plan, and so gets to vote on it.

concepts.name: Claim
concepts.one_line: What a creditor is owed, as the bankruptcy court counts it; recoveries are quoted as a percentage of the claim.

concepts.name: Recovery
concepts.one_line: What a class actually receives against its claim, in cash, new debt or equity, usually quoted in cents on the dollar.

concepts.name: Fulcrum security
concepts.one_line: The class where enterprise value runs out: the most senior impaired class, which receives the reorganized equity.

concepts.name: Take-back debt or preferred
concepts.one_line: New debt or preferred stock issued under a plan to existing lenders in satisfaction of their claims, instead of cash.

concepts.name: Ad hoc group
concepts.one_line: An informal group of holders of one instrument who hire counsel and negotiate as a block.

concepts.name: Price in points and cents on the dollar
concepts.one_line: Distressed debt trades as a percentage of face value; a bond at 40 costs forty cents per dollar of claim, and the price implies the market's recovery guess.

concepts.name: Par
concepts.one_line: The face value of a bond or loan, the 100 that prices and recoveries are measured against.

concepts.name: Credit agreement
concepts.one_line: The contract governing a bank or term loan, the loan-market cousin of an indenture, with tighter covenants and a lender group that can act faster.

concepts.name: Capital expenditure (capex)
concepts.one_line: Cash spent on long-lived assets such as terminals and ships; growth capex funded with debt is a classic cause of distress when the projects run late.

concepts.name: Adjusted EBITDA
concepts.one_line: Management's EBITDA after add-backs for items it calls one-off; creditors strip the add-backs back out before trusting a leverage ratio.

concepts.name: Refinancing
concepts.one_line: Replacing maturing debt with new debt; when the market will not refinance, a maturity becomes the event that forces a restructuring.

concepts.name: Collateral pools and non-collateral assets
concepts.one_line: Assets pledged to one lender group versus those left unpledged; unpledged assets are what a later deal can pledge to new money, ahead of everyone.

concepts.name: Drop-down
concepts.one_line: Moving assets into a subsidiary outside the existing lenders' collateral so new debt can be raised against them, priming the old lenders without touching their documents.
concepts.moyer: not in Moyer by name; extends out-of-court exchanges

concepts.name: Subsidiary issuer
concepts.one_line: A new entity created to issue debt with its own collateral, so that its lenders rank ahead of the parent's on those assets.

concepts.name: Consent fee
concepts.one_line: A cash payment to creditors for signing an RSA early or voting for a plan, the price of buying near-unanimous support.

concepts.name: Standstill fee
concepts.one_line: A payment for agreeing not to enforce remedies for a period, so a deal can be negotiated without an acceleration.

concepts.name: Holdout
concepts.one_line: A creditor who refuses to join a consensual deal hoping to be paid in full by the others, the problem that court processes exist to solve.

concepts.name: English Part 26A restructuring plan
concepts.one_line: A court-supervised compromise under English law with class voting at 75 percent by value and the power to bind a dissenting class.

concepts.name: Cross-class cramdown
concepts.one_line: A court's power to confirm a plan over a dissenting class if that class is no worse off than in the alternative.

concepts.name: Chapter 15
concepts.one_line: The U.S. Bankruptcy Code chapter for recognizing a foreign proceeding so it binds creditors and assets in the United States.

concepts.name: Centre of main interests (COMI)
concepts.one_line: Where a debtor's main insolvency proceeding belongs; picking the entity and the forum is part of the deal design.

concepts.name: Sanction hearing
concepts.one_line: The English court hearing that approves a scheme or plan; the equivalent of a U.S. confirmation hearing.

concepts.name: Absolute priority rule
concepts.one_line: In a contested plan a class must be paid in full before any junior class receives anything; consensual deals can and do depart from it.

concepts.name: Preferred stock
concepts.one_line: Equity, not debt: no maturity and no default if the dividend is skipped, but a liquidation preference ahead of common; it sits below every creditor.

concepts.name: Liquidation preference
concepts.one_line: The amount a preferred stock must receive before the common gets anything, the number that makes 'equity' still rank.

concepts.name: Mandatorily convertible preferred
concepts.one_line: Preferred stock that turns into a fixed share of the common on a date unless redeemed, so the clock is the real transfer of ownership.

concepts.name: Dilution
concepts.one_line: The shrinking of existing owners' share when new equity is issued; a plan's 'equity keeps 35 percent' is the dilution stated the other way round.

concepts.name: Non-recourse debt
concepts.one_line: Debt whose lenders can look only to a specific asset, not to the parent, so it can be left out of headline leverage and still matter.

concepts.name: Reading a post-restructuring balance sheet
concepts.one_line: Checking what the headline 'debt cut' hides: accreting preferred, non-recourse project debt, lease obligations and the pro forma consolidated total.
